findings.title: order() mixin has off-by-one legacy box ordinal
findings.body: The order() mixin sets -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group to the same value as the modern order property, but legacy box ordinal groups are 1-based while order is 0-based (the default/unset flex item is order:0 / ordinal-group:1). As written, order(1) collides with unordered items (both ordinal-group:1) and order(0) produces an invalid ordinal-group:0, so legacy WebKit/Firefox builds targeted by the -webkit-box/-moz-box display values in flexbox() will not order items the same way as modern browsers. The legacy properties should use $val + 1.

findings.title: align-items() is incomplete/invalid for the legacy syntaxes flexbox() targets
findings.body: align-items() emits -webkit-box-align but no -moz-box-align, so old Firefox using display:-moz-box from flexbox() gets no alignment at all, and it emits -ms-align-items which is not a real property (IE10 uses -ms-flex-align). It also passes modern values straight through to the legacy properties, which use start/end rather than flex-start/flex-end, so any future align-items(flex-start/flex-end) call will silently break in the legacy browsers these mixins exist to support. Add the -moz-box-align mapping (with value translation) and drop or fix the invalid -ms- property.

findings.title: Small-action button loses right alignment when container becomes flex
findings.body: Making .small-action a flex container (flexbox + align-items(center)) turns its direct-child button into a flex item, and floats are ignored on flex items, so the button's existing float:right (line 309) no longer has any effect. Nothing replaces it: .small-action-desc has no flex-grow and the button has no margin-left:auto, unlike .panel in header.scss which was given margin-left:auto for the same conversion. The dismiss/action button that previously sat at the far right of small-action rows (e.g. split/closed notices) will now sit immediately after the description text. Add margin-left:auto to the button or flex-grow:1 to .small-action-desc.

findings.title: Flex header contents has no shrink protection for long topic titles
findings.body: .contents is now display:flex, and flex items default to min-width:auto, meaning the .title/.extra-info-wrapper item cannot shrink below its content size. A long topic title shown in the docked header (via .extra-info-wrapper, ordered at topic.scss:30) can therefore force the .panel icons off the right edge or overflow the header instead of truncating, where the previous float layout constrained it. The title/extra-info flex item needs min-width:0 (with text-overflow handling on the title) to allow it to shrink within the flex row.
